title: Generate endpoint documentation using OpenAPI
description:
Enterprise only. Documents the endpoint so you can [automatically generate OpenAPI documentation](https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/) through `krakend openapi export` command.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

description.title: API Description
description.description:
An introductory, optionally verbose, explanation supporting [CommonMark](http://commonmark.org/help/) syntax. If you'd like to load an **external markdown file**, you can use flexible configuration, for instance `"description": {{include "openapi/intro.md" | toJson }}`

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

audience.title: Audience
audience.description:
The list of audiences that will consume this endpoint. These values **do not define the gateway logic** in any way. They are a way to group endpoints and filter them out when generating the OpenAPI documentation. Use `*` to indicate an endpoint will be present in any audience generated.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

custom_security_schemes.title: Custom security schemes
custom_security_schemes.description:
At the endpoint level, write only the object name with no properties inside, e.g, `{"OAuth2Security":{}`.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

^.*$.title: Security Scheme
^.*$.description: An empty object referencing a security scheme defined at the service level.

disable_default_response_definitions.title: Disable default response definitions
disable_default_response_definitions.description:
By default, KrakenD adds a `500` and a `200` response definition to each endpoint. Set this property to `true` if you want to avoid this behavior.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

example.title: Example
example.description:
**Deprecated in OAS3** (use `response_definition` instead). A free form JSON object or a string you would like to show as a sample response of the endpoint. The examples assume they are JSON content types except when using the `output_encoding=string`.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

header_definition.title: Header definition
header_definition.description:
Sets a detailed description for the headers allowed in the endpoint. Make sure to include the same headers in the endpoint's `input_headers`.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

description.title: Name
examples: The Content-Type sets the encoding of the request

type.title: Type
type.description: The type of data according to the OpenAPI spec

enum.title: Enum
enum.description: The allowed values for this header

required.title: Required
required.description: Set to `true` when this query string is required

hide.title: Hide header
hide.description: Avoids this header from showing in the generated documentation

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the header, as declared in `input_headers`

operation_id.title: Operation ID
operation_id.description:
A unique string identifying the operation identifier. Usually the method + the endpoint. If provided, these IDs must be unique among all operations described in your API.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

param_definition.title: Param definition
param_definition.description:
Sets a detailed description for the URL parameters (e.g.: `/foo/{param}`) required in the endpoint. Make sure to include to write the param exactly as in the endpoint definition.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

examples.title: Examples
examples.description: Guess what? Multiple example values for this parameter.

type.title: Type
type.description: The type of data according to the OpenAPI spec

enum.title: Enum
enum.description: The allowed values for this parameter

format.title: Format
format.description:
The extending format for the previously defined type. If the type is `number` or `string` you can apply them one of the available formats. If you choose string formats for numbers or viceversa de linter does not check it.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

required.title: Required
required.description: A path parameter is always mandatory on KrakenD, but you can still generate the OpenAPI documentation saying otherwise.

example.title: Example
example.description: An example value for this parameter. This example is injected in the spec as is.

hide.title: Hide param
hide.description: Avoids this param from showing in the generated documentation, although is still part of the endpoint definition.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the parameter, as declared in `endpoint` without the curly braces `{}`

query_definition.title: Query definition
query_definition.description:
Sets a detailed description for the query strings allowed in the endpoint. Make sure to include the same strings in the endpoint's `input_query_strings`.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

type.title: Type
type.description: The type of data according to the OpenAPI spec

enum.title: Enum
enum.description: The allowed values for this query definition

format.title: Format
format.description:
The extending format for the previously defined type. If the type is `number` or `string` you can apply them one of the available formats. If you choose string formats for numbers or viceversa de linter does not check it.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

required.title: Required
required.description: Set to `true` when this query string is required

hide.title: Hide querystring
hide.description: Avoids this querystring from showing in the generated documentation

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the querystring, as declared in `input_query_strings`

example.title: Example
example.description:
A free form JSON object or a string you would like to show as a sample response of the endpoint. The examples assume they are JSON content types except when using the `output_encoding=string`.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

request_definition.title: Definition of a request
request_definition.description:
Describes the payload needed to consume the endpoint. If a JSON Schema validation exists, it takes precedence when generating the documentation. An example use case is when you need to document a `multipart/form-data` request body.This property is an array because you can document requests with multiple content types.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

description.title: Description
description.description:
The description of the payload this endpoint accepts.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

content_type.title: Content Type
content_type.description: The content type returned by this error, e.g., `application/json`. You cannot repeat this content type in another item.

example.description:
A free form JSON object or a string you would like to show as a sample response of the endpoint. The examples assume they are JSON content types except when using the `output_encoding=string`.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

examples.title: Examples
examples.description:

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

example_schema.description: A JSON schema that describes the request format for the accepted payload in the endpoint. Use either example or example_schema, but not both.

ref.title: Reference
ref.description: The relative reference to the `components/schema` OpenAPI definition that will be used as definition of the accepted request. Notice that the path `#/components/schemas/` is not needed.

response_definition.title: Definition of errors (OAS3 only)
response_definition.description:
Describes the different status codes returned by this endpoint. Each key is the definition of the status code, represented by a string. E.g., `200` (success), `500` (internal error), etc.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

description.title: Description
description.description:
The description of this error code, e.g., `Page not found`.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

content_type.description: The content type returned by this error, e.g., `application/json`

servers.title: Servers
servers.description:
The list of servers where the API is hosted. The server URL can be a relative path, e.g., `/v1` or an absolute path. The URL might contain `{variables}`, although these are only recognized by OpenAPI and to KrakenD they are just literal strings because it does not use them.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

description.title: Description
description.description: A short description of the server URL.

url.title: URL
url.description: The URL of the server. This URL will be used as the base path for all endpoints.

variables.title: Variables
variables.description: A [Server Variable Object](https://github.com/OAI/OpenAPI-Specification/blob/main/versions/3.0.3.md#server-variable-object) according to the OpenAPI specification. The variable name is the key and the value is the default value for that variable.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description:
A short summary for the endpoint. Use the description field for the longest explanation.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/

tags.title: Tags
tags.description:
You can assign a list of tags to each API operation. If you declare tags in the `tag_definition` at the OpenAPI service level, they will have a description in the documentation. Tagged operations may be handled differently by tools and libraries. For example, Swagger UI uses tags to group the displayed operations.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/developer/openapi/
